newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps dragged higher by $7 mogas gain.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps dragged higher by $7 mogas gain.

text.p: European oil swaps were dragged higher on Monday by a $17 a tonne jump in gasoline prices.
Physical gasoline barges traded at $232 a tonne compared to $215 on Friday, hauling August swaps up a more modest $7 a tonne to trade at $219.
Other markets were less sharply higher. Brent CFDs edged up 7 cents for this week and about five for next week's dates but activity was generally slow.
Naphtha and fuel gained $1 to $2 a tonne but traders said neither were supported by strong physical demand.
"Fuel feels over valued. There has been some oil leaving the region but not enough to warrant where swaps are," said a trader at a bank.
August barges traded at $93.50 and $93.75 but cargoes were heard to have traded some $3 a tonne lower.
Lower sulphur remains in contango but barges talked 50 cents backwardation between August and September.

Gas oil and jet premiums against the IPE gas oil contract were little changed. Gas oil crack spreads against Brent held around $4.70 a barrel for the fourth and first quarters and cracks on other products were little changed.
